newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate higher on soft peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate higher on soft peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 75 basis points to 19.75 percent in early trade on Thursday in response to a weaker peso, dealers and traders said.

"The market is under pressure. Paper has been in supply since yesterday and the peso came under pressure again, after it had apparently stabilized, and that is exerting some (upside) pressure on rates," a fixed-income analyst said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso was 2.2 centavos weaker in early trade at 7.9440/7.9485 per dollar.
The analyst said secondary rates were likely to remain under pressure due to uncertainty ahead of mid-term elections in Mexico to be held on July 6.
"We shall continue to see this behavior until the elections take place or rates reach more attractive levels and lure foreign investment flows. The market is very skittish," he added.
Dealers said that anxiety had also arisen due to foreign investors bailing out of the Mexican debt market ahead of U.S. employment data due out Friday.
"The outlook for U.S. data will exert some pressure on the market and prevent rates from adjusting downwards," a trader said, adding he felt overnight rates could rise to 20.00 percent.
Other dealers said the July 2 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee to review U.S. interest rate policy would also make the market cautious.
Overnight rates on bank paper had meanwhile increased 20 basis points to 21.00 percent.
Liquidity of 1.200 billion pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations.
